title: Why US Bond Markets Are Trembling
gist: US bond market fragility late in the northern summer coincides with softening US inflation data, but the poor performance is showing up globally rather than being US-specific, undercutting the narrative that Treasuries are losing their role as anchor of the global financial system.

insights.claim: Because markets tend to be less wrong than those who comment on them regularly, the signals from bond-market fragility should be taken seriously, especially given they coincide with softening US inflation data and other high-frequency indicators.
insights.speaker: Jim O'Neill
insights.so_what: Advocates trusting price action in bonds over commentary/narrative as the more reliable read on the macro outlook — a market-signal-first heuristic for interpreting current bond weakness.
insights.quote: Since markets tend to be less wrong than those who comment on them regularly, their signals must be taken seriously, especially when they coincide with a relative softening in US inflation figures and other high-frequency economic indicators.

insights.claim: The apparent fragility of US bonds as the northern summer ends has drawn claims that sustained weakness signals the US market losing its role as anchor of the global financial system, but the author sees little evidence for this.
insights.speaker: Jim O'Neill
insights.so_what: Pushes back on the 'end of Treasury dominance' narrative, suggesting investors shouldn't over-read US bond weakness as a structural regime shift away from Treasuries as the global anchor asset.
insights.quote: Some observers will say that sustained weakness is a sign that the US market is losing its role as the anchor of the global financial system. Yet there is little evidence of this happening.
insights.locator: paragraph beginning “LONDON—As we approach the end”

insights.claim: On recent days when US bonds traded especially poorly, other markets around the world also traded poorly, indicating the weakness is a global phenomenon rather than a US-specific loss of confidence.
insights.speaker: Jim O'Neill
insights.so_what: Suggests the recent bond selloff reflects a broad global rates/risk repricing rather than an idiosyncratic US credibility problem — relevant for distinguishing systemic from US-specific risk in cross-asset positioning.
insights.quote: On recent days when US bonds have traded especially poorly, so, too, have other markets around the world.
insights.locator: paragraph beginning “LONDON—As we approach the end”

insights.claim: The end of the northern summer is often a volatile period for financial markets, and this year all eyes are on the apparent fragility of US bonds.
insights.speaker: Jim O'Neill
insights.so_what: Flags seasonal thin-liquidity volatility as a contextual factor that may be amplifying the current bond weakness beyond fundamentals.
insights.quote: As we approach the end of the northern summer, often a volatile period for financial markets, all eyes are on the apparent fragility of US bonds.
insights.locator: paragraph beginning “LONDON—As we approach the end”
